m.chalisa.do1: Golden of body, with makara-shaped earrings and a garland of pearls on his limbs, seated on a lotus, with conch and discus: meditate on Sūrya in this form.
m.chalisa.cau1: Victory to Savitā, victory, victory to Divākara, the thousand-rayed, drawn by seven horses, dispeller of darkness.
m.chalisa.cau2: You are Bhānu, Pataṅga, Marīci, Bhāskara, Savitā, Haṃsa, Sunūra and Vibhākara.
m.chalisa.cau3: You are Vivasvān, Āditya, Vikartana, Mārtaṇḍa, a form of Hari, and Virocana.
m.chalisa.cau4: You are called Ambaramaṇi, the jewel of the sky, Khaga and Ravi; the Vedas sing of you as Hiraṇyagarbha.
m.chalisa.cau5: Calling you again and again the one who lights all with a thousand rays, the hosts of sages are pleased and filled with joy.
m.chalisa.cau6: A charioteer lovely as Aruṇa, mounted on the chariot, drives its seven horses.
m.chalisa.cau7: The glory of your orb is wholly unique; I give myself to your form of radiance.
m.chalisa.cau8: Horses like Uccaiḥśravas are yoked to it; seeing them, Indra is put to shame.
m.chalisa.cau9: Mitra, Marīci, Bhānu, Aruṇa, Bhāskara, Savitā, Sūrya, Arka, Khaga, Kalikara,
m.chalisa.cau10: Pūṣā, Ravi and Āditya: taking these names, and saying Hiraṇyagarbhāya namaḥ, salutation to Hiraṇyagarbha,
m.chalisa.cau11: whoever sings the twelve names with love and bows the head twelve times,
m.chalisa.cau12: that person gains the four goals of life and destroys the heaps of sorrow, poverty and sin.
m.chalisa.cau13: This is the wonder of the salutation; this is the essence of the grace of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva.
m.chalisa.cau14: Bhānu, whoever serves you with his mind set on you has gained the eight siddhis and the nine treasures.
m.chalisa.cau15: Those who utter the twelve names have the sins of a thousand births taken away.
m.chalisa.cau16: Those of your devotees who recite your praises, their enemies meet Yama that very moment.
m.chalisa.cau17: Wealth grows, and the family with its sons; the noose of strong delusion is cut.
m.chalisa.cau18: Arka protects the head; Ravi ever dwells upon the forehead.
m.chalisa.cau19: Sūrya ever abides on the eyes; Dinakara shines over the region of the ears.
m.chalisa.cau20: Bhānu, dwell ever in the nose; Bhāskara ever guards the good of the mouth.
m.chalisa.cau21: May Parjanya stay on our lips, and the beloved Tīkṣṇa dwell within the tongue.
m.chalisa.cau22: The throat is graced by Suvarṇaretā; Tigmatejas is lovely on the shoulders.
m.chalisa.cau23: Pūṣā is on the arms and Mitra on the back; Tvaṣṭā and Varuṇa, of fair warm rays, dwell there.
m.chalisa.cau24: For the protection of both hands is Bhānumān, who guards the chest and well protects the belly.
m.chalisa.cau25: The lovely Āditya dwells in the navel; in the waist dwells Haṃsa, his mind full of joy.
m.chalisa.cau26: Gopati Savitā dwells in the thighs; Divākara dwells gladly in the hidden parts.
m.chalisa.cau27: Vivasvān guards the feet; outside ever dwells the remover of darkness.
m.chalisa.cau28: Sahasrāṃśu guards every limb. Such is this wondrous armour of protection, thoughtfully devised.
m.chalisa.cau29: Whoever holds this so in his mind, nothing in the world brings him fear.
m.chalisa.cau30: Poverty and leprosy never afflict the one who recites this in his mind.
m.chalisa.cau31: He who takes away the darkness of the world and fills it with joy by his new light,
m.chalisa.cau32: whom the hosts of planets seize but cannot blot out: to him I bow ten million times.
m.chalisa.cau33: In the world his sons are such as Manda, that is Śani, and Dharmarāja Yama, wondrous and valiant.
m.chalisa.cau34: Blessed, blessed are you, divine Dinamaṇi; gods, sages and men are ever serving you.
m.chalisa.cau35: One who, full of devotion and feeling, keeps complete discipline is freed from the delusion of worldly existence.
m.chalisa.cau36: Supremely blessed is that embodied man with whom the remover of darkness is pleased.
m.chalisa.cau37: In Māgha he is Aruṇa, in Phālguna Sūrya; in Madhu, that is Caitra, the Sun rises named Vedāṅga.
m.chalisa.cau38: In Vaiśākha his rising is counted as Bhānu; in Jyeṣṭha he is sung as Indra, and in Āṣāḍha as Ravi.
m.chalisa.cau39: In Bhādrapada he is Yama, in Āśvina Himaretā; in Kārttika Divākara is the leader.
m.chalisa.cau40: In Agahana he bears another name, and in Pauṣa he is Viṣṇu; in the intercalary month the Sun's name is Puruṣa.
m.chalisa.do2: Those who sing the Bhānu Chālīsā with love every day gain happiness and wealth of many kinds and are ever fulfilled.
